title: Seven Places to See Diwali at Its Brightest, From Ayodhya's Deepotsav to Amritsar
excerpt: Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. Ayodhya, Varanasi, Jaipur, Amritsar, Kolkata, Goa and Udaipur each celebrate differently — here is what each does best and how to choose.
body:
• Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8. Aaj Tak's seven places to experience it are Ayodhya, Varanasi, Jaipur, Amritsar, Kolkata, Goa and Udaipur.
  • Ayodhya is the spiritual centre: Deepotsav on the Saryu riverfront at Ram Ki Paidi, with the Ram Mandir and surrounding temples.
  • Amritsar pairs Diwali with Bandi Chhor Divas at the Golden Temple; Varanasi's ghats host the Ganga Aarti — but its famous Dev Deepawali comes about 15 days later, on Kartik Purnima.
  • Jaipur is for festive markets and illuminated heritage buildings, Udaipur for a slower lakeside celebration around Lake Pichola and the City Palace.

Diwali is the one week when India's cities compete in light. With the festival falling on Sunday, November 8, 2026, Aaj Tak's travel desk picked seven places where the celebration is the destination itself. The list is a good spine for a trip — each city does a different Diwali.

Ayodhya: Deepotsav on the Saryu

Ayodhya is where the festival's story lives: the city that, in the Ramayana, welcomed Rama, Sita and Lakshmana home after 14 years of exile. Its Deepotsav fills Ram Ki Paidi along the Saryu River with earthen lamps, religious ceremonies and cultural performances, as Curly Tales describes, alongside visits to the Ram Mandir and the surrounding temples. The programme and the number of lamps vary each year, so check the official Deepotsav announcements before you travel.

"With the festival falling on Sunday, November 8, 2026, Aaj Tak 's travel desk picked seven places where the celebration is the destination itself."

Varanasi: the ghats — and a date to get right

Varanasi lights its temples, homes and narrow lanes, and the ghats give a front-row seat to the Ganga Aarti and the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. One caution every guide repeats: Dev Deepawali, the city's most famous lamp festival, is not Diwali. It falls on Kartik Purnima, about 15 days after the main festival. Arrive for Diwali and you get the city's own celebration; arrive expecting Dev Deepawali and you are two weeks early.

Amritsar, Jaipur, Udaipur — and the rest of the seven

In Amritsar, Diwali coincides with Bandi Chhor Divas, the Sikh observance of Guru Hargobind Sahib's release from imprisonment and return with 52 Hindu rulers whose freedom he secured. The Golden Temple, illuminated and reflected in its sacred pool, is the centre of it. Jaipur is the shopper's Diwali: illuminated heritage buildings and festive markets across the old city. Udaipur is the slow one — palace lights on Lake Pichola, the City Palace, handicraft markets and cultural performances at venues such as Bagore Ki Haveli. Kolkata brings its own Kali Puja-season energy to the festival period, and Goa marks the season with its distinct Narakasura traditions.

Choosing and booking

TripZilla's guide suggests 2–3 days each for Ayodhya, Jaipur, Varanasi and Udaipur, and 2 days for Amritsar — enough to pair two cities in the Diwali week without rushing. Festival arrangements and access rules change year to year; confirm event schedules through official local announcements before booking around a specific celebration, and expect Ayodhya and Varanasi rooms to go first.
